Subject: Clarify metering for long-context retrieval workloads

Hi Lauren,

Quick one from procurement as we finalize the SOW. We're evaluating Redwood for a retrieval-heavy feature where we attach a ~250k-token context to a small percentage of queries (roughly 5% of calls), while the majority are short (<= 2k tokens). A couple of questions we need clarified for the vendor checklist: 

- How is billing calculated for very long context windows? Do you bill for the full context length (250k) on every call where it's attached, or is there a different model for attached documents / retrieval contexts?
- Any rounding or minimum quantum we should be aware of (e.g., rounded to nearest 1k tokens, per-request minimums)?
- If the same context is reused frequently (prefix or caching), how does that affect billing — do cached prefixes reduce billable tokens?
- Do you offer any contractual options (committed context buckets, monthly floors, or blended rates) for heavy retrieval customers?

I'm attaching our procurement requirements and an example call pattern. We need a short write-up we can include in the legal/finance package. If you can also provide a simple worked example (billing for a session with three short calls and one long-context call) that would be perfect.

Thanks,
Anna Huang
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme AI

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Clarify metering for long-context retrieval workloads

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the clear example. Short answers up front, followed by a simple worked example. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if helpful.

Summary:
- Billing model: Redwood bills for model compute which includes both input (prompt/context) tokens and output tokens. By default we charge for the full context attached to the request (input tokens) plus any output tokens.
- Caching: If you use our built-in KV/prefix caching (recommended), repeated reuse of an identical prefix within the same session will not re-charge full compute on every call — we track active cached segments and only bill for incremental decoding work.
- Rounding & quantum: We apply a scheduling/charge quantum to reduce noise on very small calls — by default charges are rounded up to the nearest 64-token quantum for GPU scheduling at the per-request level. For monthly invoices we aggregate at the token level (no additional per-request rounding after aggregation).
- Contract options: We offer context-bucket pricing for large long-context customers (measured in 256-token buckets), monthly committed floors, and blended overage rates. These are negotiable for ARR/term.

Worked example (approximate numbers; we'll provide exact math for legal):
- 3 short calls: inputs 500 tokens each, outputs 100 tokens each -> billed tokens = (3*(500+100)) = 1,800 tokens. After 64-token quantum rounding per request it stays ~1.8k aggregated.
- 1 long-context call: input context = 250,000 tokens, model input additional prompt 100 tokens, output 300 tokens -> billed tokens = 250,400 input + 300 output = 250,700 tokens.
- Total billed tokens for the session = 252,500 tokens (rounded and aggregated on monthly invoice). If the long context is mostly cached across multiple calls in the same session, the incremental bill for subsequent calls drops significantly.

We can propose a context-bucket commit to reduce billable volatility — for example: commit to 200k 256-token buckets/month (covers expected peak), with a 20% discount on bucket usage and a blended overage rate after the commit.

I'll put together the short write-up for your procurement pack and include an example invoice line and telemetry metrics to prove caching behavior. Do you need the write-up by end of week?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Lauren — quick internal note before we send the formal procurement write-up.

Acme looks like a strong mid-market ARR opportunity; they asked explicitly about bucket/commit options and rounding. I propose the following negotiable commercial construct to win the deal without setting a broad precedent: 

- Offer: 12-month commit to 200k 256-token context buckets/month (equivalent to ~51.2M context tokens/month) + standard per-token billing for non-bucket usage.
- Discount: 18% off list for committed buckets; 5% additional credit as a one-time migration credit applied in month 1.
- Quantum: keep 64-token per-request scheduling rounding but guarantee monthly aggregation is exact (no extra rounding at invoice time).
- Telemetry: require integration of our token-level telemetry agent (read-only) so they can reconcile caching benefits; acceptance of telemetry will be a Condition Precedent for the discount.

If we make the discount deeper (>=25%) legal will push for broader standardization across mid-market deals. I recommend 18% + one-time credit as a safe middle ground.

I've attached a proposed SOW that maps buckets to usage tiers and shows blended overage math (proposed_sow_acme.docx). Approve/deny and I'll push a formal commercial term to the legal template.

-rishi
Senior Sales Lead, Accounts GTM

Thanks Rishi — I agree with the construct with two adjustments before we share with procurement/legal: 

1) Discount cap: 18% committed discount is fine, but the migration credit should be a fixed $25k one-time credit (instead of a %), to avoid compounding against ARR for future renewals.
2) Term & telemetry: commit to a 12-month term with telemetry on day one. If they refuse telemetry we revert to list pricing + no discount.

Also add a short SLA clause that if caching telemetry shows less than 40% cache hit for the first 30 days we'll allow a one-time onboarding credit of $10k to cover engineering integration.

Once Rishi updates the SOW with those items I'll approve to forward. Please also add the CRM reference ACME-9421 and create a DocuSign envelope when we have the final SOW/pricing (I want sign-off by EOD Friday if possible).
